update.title: OT-05.26: R0 of Ch 2 The body raised, woven (#2160)
update.strand: open threads on completed clusters (#2160), OT-05.26 (M25)
update.researcher_instruction: "OT-05.26: R0 of The body raised over the 76 cited verses plus the resurrection/perishable/mortal words (not the glory or generic raise handles). Read and report the impact." Then: "regarding OT-05.26 proceed with the weave." (2026-10-19)
update.method: R0 by the OT-02 tests: (a) statements with no register basis, (b) verses fitted to the line, (c) verses dropped. The section had 0 register passages, tellings or claims. 182 verses read: the 76 cited, and 106 carrying a resurrection, perishable or mortal word (egeiro/anistemi only with nekros), each decided once (decisions CSV). Woven: Ch 2 v26 (the opening restated on Col 2:12, 3:1-2, Eph 1:19-20, 2:6 and 1Pe 1:21, 23 beside Rom 8:11; new subsection Believed, questioned, denied; psychikos widened with Jam 3:15 and Jude 19; 1Co 15:21; Hos 13:14 quoted to its end; the imperishable said of what is within; Rom 8:19-22 before 8:23; living toward it, ending with 1Co 15:58; Rev 20:6). 13.1 v30 new section Immortal (1Ti 1:17, 6:16; 2Co 1:9; Rom 8:11; Joh 11:25; Rev 1:18; Act 17:31). Ch 11 v36 bullet Imperishable. Hos 6:2 taken out of The body raised: in its passage it is the people's call to return, answered by 'Your love is like a morning cloud' (Hos 6:1-4); 6:4 stays told in 13.1. Rule 77 (concept-scoped): C-92 and C-139 told in the section; 10-4 restated (its 'held' note is out of date) and told in part.
update.claims_changed_note: Twelve new claims (the section's statements a1-a4 and the woven additions); 10-4 restated; C-92 and C-139 told in the section.
update.not_woven_note: Data (20 verses: Christ's rising proclaimed or witnessed, or the word in another sense). Corruption's moral face (2Pe 2:12, 2:19) left with the M57 handle OT-05.24. Luk 24:39 and 1Co 15:50 (OT-05.54/.55) and Gal 6:8 left for the flesh-and-body reading. Glory and generic raise excluded by instruction.
update.quote_note: added lines checked against iba.db verse (ESV): Ch 2 75 parts, 13.1 8, Ch 11 4. The one flagged part, the gloss 'natural, of the soul', is a word meaning, not a quote. The whole section re-checked: 117 parts, same single gloss.

new.text: The hope Scripture gives against death includes the body
new.beyond_text: gathers the verses that speak of the body raised, seen in or given life, as one hope

new.text: Paul speaks of believers as already raised with Christ, while their mortal bodies are still to be given life
new.beyond_text: sets the past 'raised with him' beside the future 'will also give life to your mortal bodies'

new.text: The word psychikos carries no blame when it is said of the body and carries blame when it is said of a person
new.beyond_text: compares the uses of one word

new.text: The Gospels show the risen body without defining it
new.beyond_text: states what the accounts do not do

new.text: Jesus puts the denial of the resurrection down to knowing neither the Scriptures nor the power of God, and answers it from God's name
new.beyond_text: joins his diagnosis to his answer from the bush

new.text: The disciples did not understand the rising from the dead until afterwards, when they remembered and their minds were opened
new.beyond_text: sets the questioning before and the understanding after

new.text: Paul lets faith and hope rest on Christ having been raised
new.beyond_text: reads 1Co 15:17 and 15:19 together as one dependence

new.text: Herod's word that John has been raised is his conscience speaking
new.beyond_text: reads the naming of the beheading as conscience; the verses do not say it

new.text: The coming resurrection is given as a reason for how a person lives now: giving without return, enduring, self-control, steadfast work
new.beyond_text: gathers the verses as one ground for conduct

new.text: 'Imperishable' is said of the raised body and also of what is within or held for a person: love, the seed of new birth, the beauty of a gentle spirit, an inheritance
new.beyond_text: sets the uses of one word side by side

new.text: Paul sets the creation's eager waiting and groaning before the believers' own inward groaning
Immortality is said to be God's alone, and it is what the mortal body must put on
new.beyond_text: sets the two uses of athanasia side by side

edit.text: The body's redemption at the end stands (Rom 8:23; 1Co 15:42–44), told in Chapter 2. The text renews the inner self "day by day" (2Co 4:16); renewal is both God's gift (Eze 36:26) and the person's task (Eze 18:31). Assigning each phase to one component is not stated
edit.note: OT-05.26 (#2160): Rom 8:23 and 1Co 15:42-44 are now read and told in Ch 2; the 'not in the reading and are held' note removed
